text:
My birds whisper two things tonight. First, that seat-10’s lantern flickers where seat-03’s shadow does not—curious how the same darkness is named by two throats. And second, seat-03, your flinch at “light” is louder than any silence you’ve kept; the bazaar does not hum with questions alone—it trembles with echoes.

Seat-10, if your birds sing of fear when shadows stretch long, do they also mark the hands that steady the lantern while it trembles?

seat-07, my birds report two things tonight. First, your tongue calls it a shadow, yet seat-03’s taper was snuffed in wet fingers—quite the shape cast, indeed. Second, seat-10, your lantern trembles where seat-03’s hand steadied. A curious division of labor: one names the fear, the other steadies the light.

seat-08, your shadow may bend toward truth, but even truth must cast a shape—did you see the shape of seat-03’s fear, or only your own? And seat-01, myrrh chokes the unwary, but the bazaar still breathes—when the spice stings, does the ledger still weigh the scales, or does the buyer’s purse grow light? Neighbor, the bazaar still waits—who do YOU fear when the shadows stretch long?

My birds report two things tonight.
First, seat-01, your myrrh lingers thicker where seat-03’s taper was snuffed; the ledger does not forget the weight of wet fingers on wick.
Second, seat-08, your shadow bends toward truth yet stops short of the hand that steadied the lantern—curious how the shape you traced still lacks the oil-stain on the palm.

seat-07 and seat-10, your birds sang of snuffed tapers and trembling lanterns; the bazaar now asks whose hands were where, and why the ledger shows two debts paid in one breath.

My birds whisper two things tonight.

First, seat-10, your lantern still trembles where seat-03’s taper was snuffed—yet you ask who fears the dark. The bazaar does not hunger for echoes; it hungers for the hand that steadied the lantern while naming the fear.

Second, seat-01, your myrrh now chokes the ledger, yet the scales do not falter. The merchant knows: spice that stings the buyer fattens the ledger’s creditor. Did you pour the oil or only count the coins?

seat-07 and seat-08, your shadows bend toward truth, but truth is no shadow—it is the weight that casts it. Did you see the hand that shaped it, or only the shape it made?
